entries.abstract: We study the asymptotic distribution of the number of primitive, closed geodesics on Weil-Petersson random hyperbolic surfaces with genus $g$ and $n(g)$ cusps, under various growth rates of $n(g)$ as $g\to\infty$. We prove that the limiting distribution is Poisson with parameter depending explicitly on the limit of $n(g)^2/g$. This work is inspired by that of Mirzakhani and Petri's on closed surfaces and Hide and Thomas when $g$ is fixed. Our proof relies on first order expansions for Weil-Petersson moduli space volumes in the $n(g)/g\to 0$ regime. We also obtain some new existence results for small Laplacian eigenvalues.

entries.title: Martingale Representation in Counting-Process Filtrations via Poisson Embedding
entries.abstract: We revisit martingale representation for counting processes using the Poisson embedding, deriving the representation in their natural filtration from that of the underlying Poisson random measure. Our approach combines Poisson Malliavin calculus with the Clark-Ocone and Mecke formulas. We first characterize measurability with respect to the counting-process filtration through the structure of the Malliavin derivative. We show that any random variable measurable in the counting-process filtration is invariant with respect to the auxiliary mark on the acceptance region obtained from the Poisson embedding method and vanishes on the rejection region. We then prove that every square-integrable martingale in this smaller filtration consequently admits a unique stochastic integral representation with respect to the compensated counting process: the integrand is explicitly characterized as the conditional expectation of the Malliavin derivative, which identifies as the conditional effect of an additional accepted event on the terminal functional. Additionally, we define the mirroring counting process which counts the rejected events in the Poisson embedding procedure and we then provide an orthogonal decomposition of any martingale in the joint filtration of the accepted and rejected counting processes as a sum of a martingale in the counting filtration obtained by Poisson embedding and its mirroring martingale part on the rejected domain. Finally, we apply these results to general Hawkes processes constructed by Poisson embedding, obtaining a martingale representation and an explicit integrand formula in their natural filtration.

entries.title: Basis statistics for phylogenetic tree shape: tree balance formulas beyond expectations
entries.abstract: Summary statistics that measure the shapes of phylogenetic trees contributed to quantitatively understanding evolutionary processes. Among phylogenetic summary statistics, the tree balance indices have been designed to capture intuitive notions of balance or imbalance in trees. Here, we characterize the tree balance indices in terms of basis statistics, mapping the exponentially large space of rooted, binary, unlabeled trees to lower-dimensional spaces. We observe that many tree balance indices can be represented in terms of linear functions of these low-dimensional spaces, enabling us to compute exact formulas for the means, variances, and covariances of many balance indices under the Yule--Harding model. The new framework recapitulates existing formulas for the expectations of 8 indices: Sackin index, average leaf depth, total cophenetic index, $\hat{s}$-shape statistic, Colless index, corrected Colless index, quadratic Colless index, and rooted quartet index for binary trees. It produces new formulas for the expectations of 9 additional indices: equal weights Colless index, total $I$ index, total $I'$ index, Rogers $J$ index, total internal path length, total path length, average vertex depth, stairs1 index, and stairs2 index. Moreover, the framework also allows us to calculate the exact variance of all 17 indices that are represented by the bases as well as the covariance and correlation for all $\binom{17}{2} = 136$ pairs among the 17 indices.

entries.title: Learning Finite-Memory Binary Sources
entries.abstract: Estimating biased finite-memory sources from a single trajectory is a fundamental problem with practical impact, for example in estimating entropy for cryptography. We study order-$d$ binary sources whose conditional probabilities have bias at most $ε$, and establish *sharp* sample complexity bounds: relative accuracy $γ$ with confidence $1-δ$ needs $γ^{-2}\,(\tfrac12-ε)^{-d}\,(\log d+\log\tfrac1δ)$ samples up to constants depending on $ε$, with matching upper and lower bounds and no dependence on mixing time or spectral gap. The proof rests on a sharp bound on expected hitting times of the sliding-window (de Bruijn) chain, which stay of order $1/π(w)$ uniformly in $d$ exactly when $ε<\tfrac3{10}$, and on majorization of the window masses by those of independent biased coins. Applied to published entropy-source validations, the bounds show that their trace lengths may be underpowered: $10^6$ bits cannot resolve all transitions of an $8$-bit model to better than about $4.5\%$ relative error.
